name: Data Vault warehouse
description: Data Vault 2.0 separates what never changes from what always does: hubs hold business keys, links hold relationships, satellites hold descriptive attributes with full load history — insert-only, hash-keyed, and source-auditable by construction. Raw vault stores data exactly as sources delivered it (audit trail included for free); business vault layers derived rules and conformity on top without touching the raw record; downstream marts (usually Kimball-style stars) serve the actual queries, because nobody should ever point BI at a vault. The pattern absorbs new sources and schema drift with minimal rework — add satellites, never alter — at the cost of an explosion in table count and joins that makes discipline and code generation non-negotiable.
when_to_use: Choose this when many volatile sources must be integrated and full auditability is a requirement, not a preference — regulated finance, insurance, healthcare, where 'show me exactly what the source said on March 3rd' is a real question.
It shines when sources change faster than modelling committees can meet, since raw vault loading is pattern-based and automatable.
Source systems change often and you need to absorb churn without remodeling.
when_not_to_use: Avoid it for analytics-first teams with a handful of stable sources — the hub/link/satellite ceremony is pure overhead there, and Kimball-on-dbt (12) delivers value months sooner.
Do not adopt without automation and at least one experienced vault modeller: hand-written vault SQL at scale is a maintenance disaster.
Query performance directly on the vault is poor by design — if you cannot afford the marts layer, you cannot afford the vault.

hot_spots.title: Modeling discipline
hot_spots.detail: Inconsistent hub, link, and satellite design erodes the audit guarantees.

hot_spots.title: Join complexity
hot_spots.detail: Vault queries explode into many-way joins; skipping marts kills BI performance.

hot_spots.title: Load ordering
hot_spots.detail: Parallel loads with wrong dependencies corrupt satellite history.

stages.name: Staging
stages.role: Land source deltas and compute hash keys and hashdiffs ready for vault loading
stages.rationale: Vault staging is where hash keys (business-key hashes) and hashdiffs (change-detection hashes) get computed, and dbt with the AutomateDV package (formerly dbtvault — no separate corpus entry, it rides on dbt) generates exactly this boilerplate from configuration. Physical landing happens upstream via your EL tool (Fivetran/Airbyte). Get hashing rules — casing, trimming, null handling, delimiter choice — standardized here and never change them; inconsistent hashing corrupts a vault irreparably.

stages.name: Raw vault
stages.role: Insert-only hubs, links, and satellites storing source data unmodified with full history
stages.rationale: Raw vault loading is deliberately mechanical — the same insert-only patterns per entity type — which is why generation beats hand-writing: dbt plus AutomateDV templates hubs, links, and satellites from metadata, keeping hundreds of tables consistent. Dedicated Data Vault automation suites (VaultSpeed, WhereScape) have no corpus entries but are worth knowing about at enterprise scale; Coalesce ships vault patterns in its GUI. The insert-only rule is sacred: no updates, no deletes, ever — that is the audit guarantee.

stages.name: Business vault
stages.role: Derived satellites, computed links, and point-in-time tables applying business rules over the raw record
stages.rationale: Business vault is where soft rules live — deduplication verdicts, computed effectivity, PIT and bridge tables that make downstream querying tractable — kept strictly separate from raw so rules can be rebuilt without touching the audit record. PIT tables deserve emphasis: they are the difference between marts that join in seconds and marts that join in hours. Still dbt/SQLMesh territory; the separation is architectural, not tooling.

stages.name: Marts
stages.role: Kimball-style stars and flat views built from the vault for actual consumption
stages.rationale: The vault is for storage and audit; marts are for people. Build dimensional stars (blueprint 12's discipline applies wholesale) from PIT-assisted vault queries with dbt, and let BI and semantic layers (Cube, Power BI models) see only this layer — vault internals leaking into reports is the classic failure smell. Because marts are fully derived, they are disposable and rebuildable, which is exactly the flexibility the vault's rigidity purchased.
